title: Telling connected stories
subtitle: Make a story move
objectives: Choose past-tense viewpoint according to narrative purpose.
Connect background and a bounded event.
Retell an event with clarification and an ending.
warmup: Retrieve two sentences and one repair strategy from c2-u08. Change the subject or situation in each sentence and explain what changed. Then read today’s objectives and predict where your existing language may be insufficient.

lectures.title: Background and advancing events
lectures.body: Mientras caminaba, vi a Ana presents walking as the ongoing background and seeing Ana as a bounded event. The distinction is viewpoint, not action length: Trabajé allí veinte años can bound a long period; estaba un momento en la puerta can describe a brief scene. Habit words do not force imperfect in every context: De niño jugaba allí describes a habit, while Durante aquel verano jugué allí todos los días bounds the series. Ask whether you are setting the scene, presenting a recurring situation, or advancing the sequence with an event.

lectures.title: Change the viewpoint, change the message
lectures.body: Conocía a Ana says I already knew her; conocí a Ana often presents meeting her. Sabía la respuesta describes knowledge; supe la respuesta can present learning it. No quería salir describes a state of reluctance; no quise salir can present a bounded refusal. These are tendencies in context, not memorized one-to-one translation equations. Plan a story in three parts: setting, complication and outcome. Use a repair phrase if your listener loses the timeline: Primero…, antes de eso…, lo que pasó después fue…. Retelling from another viewpoint helps reveal what each tense contributes.

lectures.title: Read the same event through two lenses
lectures.body:
Compare **Cuando llegué, Ana preparaba café** with **Cuando llegué, Ana preparó café**. The first normally presents preparation as already in progress at the moment of arrival. The second presents the arrival and preparation as events in the sequence; it can suggest that she made coffee afterward. Do not choose a tense merely because **cuando** appears. Decide what relationship you want to communicate.

The same distinction affects summaries. **La reunión era larga** describes its character from within the situation. **La reunión fue larga** evaluates the meeting as a completed whole. Both can be grammatical descriptions of a real meeting; their viewpoints differ. A quiz must supply enough context to make the requested viewpoint clear. In your own writing, you can create that context.

Revise a story by underlining background in one style and bounded events in another. If every sentence is background, the listener may wait for something to happen. If every sentence advances the plot, the listener may lack a reason or setting. Good narration uses both to make the event understandable.

reading: Era viernes y llovía. Lucía esperaba el autobús cuando vio una cartera en el suelo. La recogió y buscó un nombre. Mientras miraba una tarjeta, llegó un hombre que parecía preocupado. «Perdí la cartera», dijo. Lucía no se la entregó inmediatamente: primero le pidió que describiera su contenido. El hombre dio los detalles correctos y ella se la devolvió. Después llegó el autobús. Lucía conocía el barrio, pero nunca había hablado con aquel vecino. Identifica el escenario, los sucesos que avanzan la historia y la razón de pedir una descripción.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: While I was walking, I saw Ana.
quiz.explanation: “Mientras caminaba, vi a Ana” expresses “While I was walking, I saw Ana”. “Después se la devolví” instead means “Afterward I returned it to him or her”. “Ya sabía la respuesta” instead means “I already knew the answer”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: It was Friday and it was raining.
quiz.explanation: “Era viernes y llovía” expresses “It was Friday and it was raining”. “Supe la respuesta después” instead means “I found out the answer afterward”. “Parecía preocupado” instead means “He seemed worried”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: I met Ana yesterday.
quiz.explanation: “Conocí a Ana ayer” expresses “I met Ana yesterday”. “No quería salir” instead means “I did not want to go out as a background state”. “¿Qué pasó al final?” instead means “What happened in the end?”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: I already knew Ana.
quiz.explanation: “Ya conocía a Ana” expresses “I already knew Ana”. “No quise salir” instead means “I refused or chose not to go out in that episode”. “Mientras caminaba, vi a Ana” instead means “While I was walking, I saw Ana”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: I worked there for twenty years as a bounded period.
quiz.explanation: “Trabajé allí veinte años” expresses “I worked there for twenty years as a bounded period”. “Era viernes y llovía” instead means “It was Friday and it was raining”. “Ya sabía la respuesta” instead means “I already knew the answer”.

quiz.prompt: Match each English meaning to its Spanish expression. Use each expression once.
answers: ["Trabajé allí veinte años","Primero recogí la cartera","Después se la devolví"]
quiz.explanation: “Trabajé allí veinte años” means “I worked there for twenty years as a bounded period”. “Primero recogí la cartera” means “First I picked up the wallet”. “Después se la devolví” means “Afterward I returned it to him or her”. Each alternative belongs to a different meaning; check the whole phrase, including its grammatical person and register.

homework.prompt: Read the original text for this unit. Identify its situation, central message, and three supporting details. Then write a new version of 100–140 words for a different person or audience. Use the target patterns, change at least three facts, and explain two revisions.
homework.model:
Era viernes y llovía. Lucía esperaba el autobús cuando vio una cartera en el suelo. La recogió y buscó un nombre. Mientras miraba una tarjeta, llegó un hombre que parecía preocupado. «Perdí la cartera», dijo. Lucía no se la entregó inmediatamente: primero le pidió que describiera su contenido. El hombre dio los detalles correctos y ella se la devolvió. Después llegó el autobús. Lucía conocía el barrio, pero nunca había hablado con aquel vecino. Identifica el escenario, los sucesos que avanzan la historia y la razón de pedir una descripción.

This is the source model, not a text to submit unchanged. A successful adaptation retains the communicative purpose while changing relevant forms and facts. Compare with the worked examples for the reasons behind form choices.
homework.rubric: 0–3 each: fulfills the specified purpose; organized and comprehensible; target forms support meaning; revisions are explained with examples. 0 = no evidence, 1 = substantial help needed, 2 = effective with some support, 3 = independently effective for this task. Record who evaluated the work.

homework.prompt: Complete the resource assignment, or ask a willing reader to read the original text without showing it to you. First listen for the situation and purpose; listen again for three details and one contrast. Write a 60–100-word listening log naming the source, words actually heard, one uncertainty, and how you checked it. If using local synthesized speech, label it synthetic. Text-only preparation is not completed listening.
homework.model: A useful log separates the speaker’s message from your interpretation: “I heard [specific phrase]; I understood [claim]; I was uncertain about [word/relationship]; checking [text or partner] changed my interpretation to [correction].” Use the unit reading as an answer reference for a read-aloud version, never as evidence of an external speaker’s words.
homework.rubric: 0–2 each: identifies source and listening conditions; retrieves central meaning; supports three details; checks a specific uncertainty. Do not count a copied transcript as independent comprehension.

homework.prompt: Tell a story with a setting, complication and outcome. Your partner interrupts twice to ask when or why. Retell it in writing and explain three tense choices.
homework.model: Use the original reading/dialogue and the sentence-pattern cards as preparation. Make a brief outline, then put it away. Your partner should introduce a detail you did not prepare. Respond, request clarification if needed, and summarize what you agreed or still disagree about. Solo fallback: record two possible viewpoints and improvise a response after a pause; label it rehearsal.
homework.rubric: 0–3 each: task fulfillment, comprehensibility, control of target language, responsiveness to another speaker. A partner or instructor should cite one example per score. Solo rehearsal provides no evidence for live responsiveness; mark that dimension not observed.

homework.prompt: On a later day, retrieve six cards without looking. Use three in a fresh response to the practical task. Identify one recurring form error and one communication difficulty. Produce a corrected example, explain the reason, and schedule a specific follow-up exchange or listening session.
homework.model: Compare your response with these two models: Mientras caminaba, vi a Ana / Era viernes y llovía. A useful reflection explains the function, not just the spelling. Revisit the first worked item and create a different example of its principle.
homework.rubric: Report recall count separately from performance. Reflection is complete when it contains an observed difficulty, an explained correction, a fresh example, and an actionable next session.

task: Tell a story with a setting, complication and outcome. Your partner interrupts twice to ask when or why. Retell it in writing and explain three tense choices.
culture: Narrative conventions vary, but listeners everywhere benefit from clear reference and sequence. Avoid presenting your interpretation of a stranger’s motives as an established fact; use parecía or según dijo when appropriate.
selfAssessment: I can choose past-tense viewpoint according to narrative purpose.
I can connect background and a bounded event.
I can retell an event with clarification and an ending.
remediation: Sort mistakes by form, meaning, and interaction. For form errors, explain a worked example and create a contrasting pair. For comprehension errors, replay a short segment or use a willing reader and verify your interpretation. For interaction difficulties, repeat the practical task with one new constraint. Compare evidence across days; repeated selection of a known answer alone is not mastery.
